messages.subject: Making Predictions with 2-parameter Logistic Model
parts:
Hello Everyone,

I'd like to use the 2-parameter Logistic Model model to compute the probability of student $i$ getting question $j$ correctly. I wonder if I can achieve this by calculating the fscores and coef, both with oblimin rotation :

> model <- mirt(df, 2, itemtype= "2PL", SE=TRUE)
> latent_traits <-  fscores(models, method = "EAP", response.pattern= df %>% as.matrix(), full.scores = TRUE, rotate = "oblimin")
> coefs_est <- coef(model, rotate="oblimin")

Specifically, do the variables latent_traits and coefs_est exactly refer to the $\theta$ and $\alpha$ parameters in the 2-parameter logistic model equation ? 
$$\frac{1}{1+ \exp \{-(\alpha_1 * \theta_1+ \alpha_2 * \theta_2 + d) \}}$$

My results seem reasonable when I assume this, but I want to make sure if this is correct. Thank you very much.

Best,
Jiguang

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: Making Predictions with 2-parameter Logistic Model
parts:
Yes, this looks fine to me. Though you may have better luck with the probtrace() functions and after replacing the slopes from the extracted items directly. Something like 

item <- extract.mirt(mod, 1)
item@par[1:2] <- slopes_from_rotation
probtrace(item, Theta)

Or something to that effect. HTH.

Phil
